I have always been against ideas of this nature in the past. However since the admins are working on features to help mitigate brigading, the time to seriously consider this level of transparency may be close.

It might seem like a good idea at first, but there are some worrying negatives: public voting records would make users less comfortable voting how they want to for fear of being audited (porn, for example). Witch hunts are already a problem; having access to someone's voting record would add fuel to the fire. It strips away a level of privacy for very little tangible gain, which is a problem in itself. It would be much easier for an individual or corporation to build a profile on your user account. It could lead to users trying to use each other's records to discredit a comment (ad hominem) which we see enough of with comment records already.

I'm happy with my comments being public, but I think upvotes and downvoats are too personal a thing to make public. At that point you're not looking at what I say about an issue, but looking directly at what I think. I should always have the choice of keeping my thoughts private.

I think it's impossible to achieve any real manner of meritocracy.

As far as the quest for such goes, I'd say that generational wealth is certainly a counter-force, but I'd say that it's not the most notable one. The most notable one, and the reason that I say the achievement of a meritocracy is impossible anyway, is the fact that, one way or another, the authority necessary to maintain the system will be placed in the hands of humans, and humans are corruptible and shortsightedly self-serving.

And I should note that, since I consider the corruptibility and shortsighted self-servingness of humans to be fundamental qualities, I would oppose any attempt anyone might propose to counter the threat that generational wealth would pose to a meritocracy because it's been amply demonstrated, with no exceptions, that corruptible and shortsightedly self-serving humans granted the authority to nominally act against generational wealth can and will warp their actions such that they simply further their own shortsighted self-interest and multiply the harm that they can and will do.

So, there's two parts to this question that need to be addressed:

(1) Is it possible to have a meritocracy? Yes, and no. Let us first address the latter. As it stands, a meritocracy is impossible in terms of society's collective values. We live in a caste system in which the oligarchical rulers use all sorts of propaganda to make the lower classes believe that if they work hard enough, that they, too, will enjoy the fruits of their labor. This is a myth in which the working poor are brainwashed into believing that work ethic actually matters. Sure, every once in a while, a person who has come from nothing will realize their dreams. But these are rare exceptions to the overall rule. As George Carlin so eloquently put it: "they call it the American dream because you'd have to be asleep to believe it."

(2) Alternatively, in addressing the former, it could be possible to have something as close to a meritocracy as one could get. But this would require the global community to reassess its values, make compromises, and sacrifices. Life is a lottery. You could hit the jackpot as the offspring of someone in power and/or you could hit the jackpot as someone who is genetically predisposed to have talents that would help them maintain the power that they have inherited physically, genetically, or both. So, here is where the compromises and sacrifices need to be made. Estate taxes? They need to be at least 90%. Procreation? You should be required to apply for a parental license to bear children, the same way adoptive and foster parents need to be cleared, the same way you need licenses for all sorts of behaviors that need to be regulated: guns, hunting, fishing, driving, marriage, pets, etc. If we want a meritocracy, then we are going to have to accept eugenics as, not only a way to ensure that children who are being brought into this world will have greater odds of success on their own merits, but also as the only logical way to control the explosive overpopulation.

But #2 will never happen. So, you better start getting used to #1. ----> (Edit: typographical error.)
